title: 'Teams are moving to new models almost as fast as labs release them': Vercel data reveals AI models now have a half-life of just six weeks — with most most AI traffic running on models less than two months old
summary: Vercel data reveals AI models now have a half-life of just six weeks
detailed: Vercel's November 2026 AI Gateway Production Index report reveals that AI models have a half-life of just six weeks, with teams switching to newer models on average every four weeks.
Anthropic models dominated paid usage in October 2026, with Claude Opus 5.5 leading by spend at just over 14% and Sonnet 5.5 capturing 26% of usage.
Nearly 17% of development teams adopted models available for under two weeks by September 2026, and video model adoption grew to one in six teams.
This rapid churn matters because it highlights how easily developers switch environments between competing model releases, driving high initial usage intensities that quickly fade.
sentences: The time spent with a new AI model is decreasing, with teams using paid AI services sticking with a new model for an average of four weeks.
At that point, they switch to another new model, aiming to keep their AI code development or agents competitive.
Vercel’s AI Gateway Production Index report for November 2026 claims this trend indicates that AI models effectively have a half-life of around six weeks.
At that point, attention and use of the model decreases as teams and developers proceed to switch to the latest shiny alternative.
Illustrating the trend, Vercel reports that Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 was the top model by spend in its first full month, following its launch on September 22, 2026.
While the concept of an AI model having a half-life may initially seem outlandish, it actually makes perfect sense.
Vercel’s analysis of token transactions via its gateway shows that teams adopt new models within days of them being launched.
Assuming the use of a code editor or tool wrapper, pointing a development environment to a new model can be achieved relatively painlessly.
Vercel’s data breaks down the adoption rate into 00-14 days, 15-30 days, and 31-60 days, and highlights a trend towards increased early adoption from June 2026 onward.
By September, almost 17% were using models that had been available for under two weeks.
But older models are retained to some degree, but these are typically relying on less usage and, consequently, token spend.

So, with new models being released relatively regularly by competing AI platforms, and with easy model switching essentially baked into developers environments, they’re being used with an initial intensity that wanes when the next model launches.

Hence Vercel’s determination that models “have a half-life of about six weeks.”
Vercel also determined that the top model by spend in its first full month in October was Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5, drawing just over 14% in spend.
Meanwhile, the most widely used paid models are dominated by Anthropic.
Sonnet 5.5 (26%), Haiku 5.5 (22%), Haiku 4.5 (20%), and Opus 5.5 (18%) are the most widely-used, although there is duplication, with many team apparently relying on multiple models.
Significantly, image and video generation was also prominent, with more spend and adoption than in previous months.
One in six AI development teams are now using a video model, up from 10% in previous months.
This is where OpenAI had a rare chance to shine in Vercel's report, with its GPT-Image-2.5 Sunburst leading in image generation model spend during October.
